$comment: THIRD-PARTY RESEARCH FINDINGS we cite, each with its source and method.
SEPARATE FROM spec-facts.json ON PURPOSE. That file holds vendor pricing and
limits, which change without notice and carry a 90/180-day staleness clock.
These are published studies. A study does not go stale in 90 days; it is
superseded when the next edition appears. Different lifecycle, different file.
THE RULE. Every figure here was read off the source page and verified, not
taken from a research summary. Two figures in the dossier these came from
were nearly rejected as fabricated during verification, and both turned out
correct: one number coincidentally matched an unrelated row, and one differed
only by a thousands separator. Check against the source itself, and check
carefully, because a wrong rejection is as bad as a wrong acceptance.
CORRELATION IS NOT OUR RESULT. The framework and CMS breakdowns describe
sites built on those technologies across a million-page sample. They are not
statements about work we did, and must never be written as though they were.
Nothing here may be phrased as evidence that our builds are more accessible.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Anything the source did not state a method for.
Roughly a third of the research dossier these came from was flagged
UNVERIFIED METHOD by its own author; none of that is here.

wcag-failure-rate-2026.publisher: WebAIM, Institute for Disability Research, Policy and Practice, Utah State University
wcag-failure-rate-2026.statement: 95.9% of the top one million home pages had detected WCAG 2 failures, up from 94.8% in 2025
wcag-failure-rate-2026.note: The rise reversed six consecutive years of small improvements, which is the finding rather than the headline number.
wcag-failure-rate-2026.method: Automated evaluation with the WAVE stand-alone API against the rendered DOM after scripting and styles were applied. Sample: 1,000,000 home pages, tested February 2026.
wcag-failure-rate-2026.limitation: Automated testing detects a subset of WCAG failures. A page with no detected errors is not necessarily conformant.

errors-per-page-2026.statement: 56,114,377 distinct errors were detected across the sample, an average of 56.1 per home page
errors-per-page-2026.method: Same sample and tooling as the conformance figure. 1,000,000 home pages, February 2026.
errors-per-page-2026.limitation: Counts detected errors, not user impact. One error can affect many users and many errors can affect none.

cms-errors-2026.statement: By content management system, WordPress home pages (252,302 sampled) averaged 52.8 detected errors, Drupal (18,222) 41.2, Wix (3,183) 33.3 and Squarespace (2,669) 33.0
cms-errors-2026.note: Squarespace and Wix scored BETTER than WordPress here. Publish that as readily as the rest: a hosted builder constrains what a site owner can break, and pretending otherwise would be the kind of selective citation this site exists not to do.
cms-errors-2026.method: CMS detected per home page, errors averaged within each group. 1,000,000 home page sample, February 2026.
cms-errors-2026.limitation: Association, not causation. CMS choice correlates with site age, budget and builder skill, none of which were controlled for.

framework-errors-2026.statement: By JavaScript framework, Next.js home pages (23,863 sampled) averaged 40.9 detected errors, 27.1% below the sample average, with Astro at 9.0 and React at 43.5
framework-errors-2026.note: DO NOT write this as evidence that our builds are more accessible. It describes 23,863 sites we did not build, and almost certainly reflects that Next.js sites skew newer and better resourced. It is context for a platform choice, not proof about our work.
framework-errors-2026.method: Framework detected per home page, errors averaged within each group. 1,000,000 home page sample, February 2026.
framework-errors-2026.limitation: Association, not causation, and the sample is home pages only.

ecommerce-errors-2026.statement: Among ecommerce platforms, Shopify home pages (42,516 sampled) averaged 75.1 detected errors, 33.9% above the sample average, with Magento at 75.8
ecommerce-errors-2026.method: Platform detected per home page, errors averaged within each group. 1,000,000 home page sample, February 2026.
ecommerce-errors-2026.limitation: Association, not causation. Ecommerce home pages are more complex than the sample average, which alone raises error counts.

top-failure-types-2026.statement: Six failure types accounted for 96% of all detected errors. Low contrast text appeared on 83.9% of home pages, missing alternative text on 53.1%, and missing form input labels on 52.8%
top-failure-types-2026.note: The useful part for a site owner is that the most common failures are also the cheapest to fix.
top-failure-types-2026.method: Failure types counted across the 1,000,000 home page sample, February 2026.
top-failure-types-2026.limitation: Automated detection. Contrast and missing alt text are reliably machine-detectable; many other failure types are not.

ada-federal-filings-fy2025.publisher: Administrative Office of the United States Courts
ada-federal-filings-fy2025.statement: Federal district courts recorded 9,718 civil filings under the nature-of-suit code ADA-Other in the twelve months ending 30 September 2025, up from 9,030
ada-federal-filings-fy2025.note: Filings, not judgments, and the code covers more than website accessibility. Report it as filing volume and never as legal advice or as a prediction that any given business will be sued.
ada-federal-filings-fy2025.method: Case counts by nature-of-suit code, twelve months ending 30 September 2025.
ada-federal-filings-fy2025.limitation: ADA-Other is a broad code. It is not a count of web accessibility lawsuits specifically.

nextjs-adoption-2026.study: Usage statistics and market share of Next.js
nextjs-adoption-2026.statement: Next.js is used by 4.2% of websites whose JavaScript library is known, which is 3.2% of all websites
nextjs-adoption-2026.note: Cite this WITH the Sanity figure, never alone. The asymmetry is the point: the framework is mainstream and the CMS beside it is not.
nextjs-adoption-2026.method: Detection by signature across W3Techs' survey of the top 10 million sites. The 4.2% denominator is sites with an identified JavaScript library; the 3.2% denominator is all surveyed sites.
nextjs-adoption-2026.limitation: Detection by signature, so sites that strip their fingerprint are absent. Share of existing sites is not share of new builds.

sanity-adoption-2026.study: Usage statistics and market share of Sanity
sanity-adoption-2026.statement: Sanity is used by less than 0.1% of all websites whose content management system is known
sanity-adoption-2026.note: This is the figure that stops us writing that the stack is 'gaining popularity'. W3Techs does not publish a number below 0.1%, so there is no trend to report either, and claiming momentum for it would be unsupportable. Publish it as readily as anything else: a reader evaluating this stack should know the CMS is niche before committing, and hiring and continuity risk follow from that.
sanity-adoption-2026.method: Detection by signature across W3Techs' survey of the top 10 million sites, among sites with an identified CMS.
sanity-adoption-2026.limitation: Below the publisher's reporting threshold, so no exact value or trend is available. Headless CMSs are also harder to fingerprint than server-rendered ones, which may understate them.
